name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Mortise Channel Spike
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Mortise Channel Spike
description:
The Mortise Channel Spike is a physical-access communication device designed to establish a hardened, off-mesh encrypted channel by directly interfacing with a building's structural wiring — power conduit, data trunk, or legacy copper telephony infrastructure. A hardened tungsten spike approximately 22cm long, it is driven into any accessible wiring surface and immediately begins negotiating a carrier signal through whatever electrical medium it finds, converting ambient current fluctuations into a low-bandwidth but extremely secure transmission channel. Arcturus Defense Solutions developed it for their tactical breach teams, who needed a communication solution that would function inside signal-suppressed or Faraday-shielded structures where mesh connectivity was unavailable or compromised.

The Spike's encryption layer uses a rolling hardware cipher generated by a physical entropy chip inside the device body — a chip that cannot be interrogated without destroying it, making key extraction forensically impossible after the fact. Two Spikes negotiating on the same electrical system will find each other within 40 seconds and establish an encrypted duplex channel that carries voice at low fidelity and text at full bandwidth. The channel is entirely invisible to wireless surveillance systems and requires physical access to the building's wiring to intercept — a significant operational barrier in most environments.

In the field, the Mortise Spike has developed a reputation for being the communication tool of last resort and, paradoxically, of highest operational security. Using one requires proximity to infrastructure and leaves physical evidence, but it produces a channel that is essentially immune to the city's ubiquitous wireless monitoring. Arcturus sells it exclusively to licensed defense and security contractors, but units surface regularly in the hands of individuals for whom wireless communications have become a liability they can no longer accept.

specifications.dimensions: 22cm spike, 4cm diameter handle with integrated controls
specifications.compatible_infrastructure: AC power conduit (110–480V), structured data cabling, legacy copper telephony, grounding systems
specifications.channel_negotiation_time: 40 seconds average between two active Spikes
specifications.transmission_bandwidth: Low-fidelity voice (4kbps) and full-bandwidth text/data (up to 128kbps)
specifications.encryption: Rolling hardware cipher, physical entropy chip — non-extractable
specifications.range: Limited by building wiring topology; typically entire structure and adjacent connected infrastructure
specifications.battery_life: Passive — draws minimal power from host wiring; indefinite operation

tactical_use: Deployed in pairs — one Spike placed at an entry or staging point, one carried by the operator inside a target structure. Used when mesh communications are compromised by jamming, Faraday shielding, or hostile signal monitoring. Also used for pre-operation dead drop communication, where both parties agree on a building's electrical infrastructure as their channel. Leaves a physical mark on whatever surface it's driven into, which is a known operational liability.
cultural_context: The Mortise Spike carries a distinctly military pedigree in GLMZ's underworld — seeing one in someone's kit suggests either Arcturus training or serious operational experience. It is not a discreet or convenient device, and choosing to use one signals that the user has decided wireless is no longer an acceptable risk. Among security professionals, it is respected as a piece of engineering that prioritizes function over all other concerns. The physical evidence problem is considered a feature by some — it forces operational discipline.
story_hooks: A Mortise Spike is found still active in the wiring of a building that burned down three weeks ago — it's still receiving, and something on the other end keeps trying to transmit.

Two Spikes have been placed in the same building's infrastructure by different parties who don't know about each other. Both channels are now sharing the same carrier, and each party can hear fragments of the other's communications.

A corporate security team is tracking Spike placement patterns across GLMZ — someone has been systematically wiring up buildings in a specific district, and the pattern suggests they're building a hardwired communication network that bypasses the mesh entirely.

The players need to communicate inside a fully signal-suppressed facility. The only option is a pair of Mortise Spikes — but driving one into the building's wiring will trigger a structural current alarm they'll need to defeat first.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutal, utilitarian spike approximately the length of a hand. The business end is a sharpened tungsten point with shallow grooves for grip during impact. The handle is a reinforced composite cylinder with aggressive knurling, designed for gloved operation. Industrial, purposeful, resembling a specialized climbing tool or demolition implement rather than consumer electronics.
physical_description.dimensions: 22cm overall length; 4cm diameter handle; spike tapers to 8mm point
physical_description.weight_description: 280g — hefty enough to drive with one strong strike, but pocketable on a load-bearing tactical rig or tool belt
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten carbide spike; titanium-reinforced composite handle; embedded stainless steel reinforcement collar at transition point
physical_description.finish: Spike: gunmetal gray with light machine marks and a dull matte polish. Handle: textured rubberized non-slip coating in deep charcoal with visible wear patterns from gloved use. Collar: polished to a satin sheen.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic industrial grays and blacks. Single accent: a tiny Φ (QUANTA) currency symbol laser-etched near the handle base in faint red.
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimal: recessed pressure sensor pad (4mm diameter) on handle face for activation/negotiation. Tiny status LED (amber/green) embedded below the sensor, visible only in darkness. Micro-port for forensic drain (standard Arcturus Defense connector) hidden beneath a tungsten dust cap.
distinctive_features: Shallow helical grooves running down the spike shaft — both for grip during insertion and to facilitate current flow across varied wiring gauges
Asymmetric handle knurling: rough on one side (striking face) and smoother on the opposite (grip face) for directional impact control
Arcane Arcturus Defense logo (a stylized shield-and-spike motif) laser-marked on the handle in barely-visible dark gray
Faint manufacturing serial number and batch code stamped on the collar in tiny characters
A single drop of dried sealant visible near the handle-shaft junction — evidence of field repair or environmental sealing
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions corporate logo on handle. Faint text: 'MORTISE CHANNEL SPIKE' and regulatory certification stamps (defense contractor only). QUANTA price equivalent etched discretely.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn but functional. Micro-scratches and scoring on the spike from contact with conduit materials. Handle shows polishing wear from repeated gloved deployment. The pressure sensor may show faint dust or corrosion from damp breaches. Field units often have improvised grip tape or electrical tape wrapping added by operators.
